ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi n°2016-1691 du 9 décembre 2016 (Sapin II); Code monétaire et financier (CMF) art. L.561-1 à L.561-50, art. L.561-2-2 (définition du bénéficiaire effectif) et art. R.561-1 et seq.; Décret n°2020-118 du 12 février 2020; Code de commerce art. L.123-31 (Registre du commerce et des sociétés) and Décret n°84-406 (RCS); Code du travail art. L.5321-1 à L.5325-5 (licence des agences de placement et entreprises de travail temporaire); Règlement (UE) n°2015/847 on wire-transfer transparency; Règlement (UE) 2024/1624 (AMLR) and Directive (UE) 2024/1640 (AMLD6) — transition period before full national application

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Certificate of Incorporation and good-standing certificate of the ultimate foreign parent entity (PRC corporate group)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PRC Market Regulation Administration (地方市场监督管理局) plus a Chinese Notary Public (公证处)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961, in force for the PRC since 7 November 2023); consular legalization remains the residual path for non-Convention origin documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (POA) appointing the resident gérant of the French SARL and the registered-agent signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; where the POA signatory is in a non-Hague state, French consular legalization (légalisation consulaire) at the French Embassy or Consulate applies

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified clear copies of passports of all UBOs holding 25% or more, of the proposed gérant, and of the AML compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chinese Notary Public (公证处) with authentication by the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs or its delegated provincial office

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation (traduction assermentée) of the entire notarized corporate, POA, passport, and apostille bundle
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator (traducteur expert) registered with a French Cour d'appel or the Cour de cassation list
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Translator's sworn certification is accepted by the greffe and the financial intelligence stakeholders without an additional apostille; the underlying source deeds remain apostilled

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of every UBO, the gérant, all authorized signatories, and the AML compliance officer against (i) the TRACFIN national asset-freezing list (listes nationales de gel d'avoirs), (ii) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list published in the Official Journal of the European Union, (iii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List, (iv) the OFAC SDN list as best practice given USD/Wise rails, and (v) the French PEP directory and international PEP databases. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is mandatory for any politically exposed person, family member, or close associate under CMF art. L.561-10. Continuous monitoring is required on a risk-based schedule aligned with GAFI/FATF Recommendations 10 and 12, with a mandatory obligation to file a déclaration de soupçon with TRACFIN for any reasonable suspicion.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the DGFiP (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) with the RCS lodged at the competent greffe du tribunal de commerce; name-conflict verification searches via Infogreffe (https://www.infogreffe.fr) and the INPI corporate and trademark database (https://data.inpi.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official filings must be in French pursuant to the Toubon law (Loi n°94-665). The corporate name (dénomination sociale) must be expressed in Latin characters; Chinese ideographic script alone is inadmissible for RCS registration. A Latin alphabetic transliteration is mandatory for the legal name, while the commercial trade name may separately be deposited in Chinese characters as a trademark at the INPI. The legal name must not be misleading as to legal form and must be followed by 'SARL' and the registered capital on official letterheads.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Bank, Crédit, Finance — prior authorization from the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) required
Assurance, Réassurance, Mutuelle — prior ACPR agrément required
Fonds, Gestion de portefeuille, Placement financier — prior AMF authorization required
État, République, France, National, Ministère, Ambassade, Consulat — misleading state or public institutional affiliation, prohibited
Avocat, Notaire, Huissier de justice, Expert-comptable — reserved regulated professions, prohibited without the corresponding title
Pharmacie, Médecin, Clinique — reserved health-profession tokens, prohibited
Travail temporaire, Intérim, Agence de placement — permissible only after the DREETS prior declaration and staffing agency licence is obtained; triggers mandatory licensing evidence
EOR, Global Employment, Payroll — no prohibition, but must not falsely imply regulated banking or official approvals
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: French law does not operate a formal registry 'reservation' of company names; the 30-day window denotes the conventional validity of the pre-clearance search and the imperative to complete RCS filing expeditiously. Upon a greffier's refusal: (i) within 15 days of notification, submit a reasoned coordination request to the same greffier accompanied by an updated INPI data search and, if available, a notarized written consent of the conflicting prior-right holder; (ii) if refused again, file a formal requête before the judge delegated by the president of the tribunal de commerce under Code de commerce art. R.123-93 within 10 days of the second refusal; (iii) alternatively, withdraw and re-file through the guichet unique with a secondary name at no additional penalty, provided the filing occurs within the 30-day window; (iv) where refusal rests on trademark likelihood of confusion, simultaneously initiate a coexistence or opposition procedure before the INPI. There is no extension of the 30-day practice window, and after expiry the selected name may lawfully be registered by a third party.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted under Code de commerce art. L.123-11-2 through a commercial domiciliation contract with an approved domiciliataire (agréé par la préfecture). For the Global EOR / Staffing Agency scope (ISIC 7810 / NAF 78.10Z), the RCS accepts a domiciliated registered office. However, the administration and the DREETS jointly treat a bare mailbox with high suspicion: the tax authorities may challenge substance under the 'boîte aux lettres' doctrine, and the staffing agency licence requires verifiable operational management. Recommended structure: a virtual office at an accredited business center for RCS purposes plus a real operational address, a French resident gérant with employment/payroll delegation, and a local payroll compliance officer.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 40% composite risk of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months: approximately 25% probability of an unannounced Urssaf audit immediately after the first payroll declaration cycle, 15% probability of a labour-inspectorate (Inspection du travail / DREETS) compliance visit concerning the staffing licence and EOR employment contracts; the addition of a pure virtual office with no operational reception adds 10 percentage points. A documented domiciliation with a physical reception desk, dedicated French payroll administration, and a resident compliance officer reduces the assessed likelihood to the 20–25% band.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 for SARL; Articles R.123-1 et seq. for RCS registration; Labour Code Articles L.124-1 et seq. for regulated employment-placement and temporary-work activity, as applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, filed electronically through the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (INPI platform).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire M0 (déclaration de constitution d'une société commerciale) submitted with signed statuts and required annexes through the Guichet Unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Article L.223-2 of the French Commercial Code. The Articles of Association may fix a lower or higher nominal capital; for regulated employment activities the capital should be sufficient to support the financial guarantee obligation under Labour Code Article L.124-3 et seq. The subscribed cash capital must be deposited into a blocked French bank account and evidenced by a bank certificate; funds are released only after RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that each shareholder's subscription to the statutory capital of the Company, as set forth in the Articles of Association, is approved and the paid-up share capital has been duly subscribed and evidenced by the bank certificate of blocked funds. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is established at [Address], France, and that all legal notices and registrations shall be submitted to the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés through the Guichet Unique. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Gérant for an indefinite term, with authority to act alone as legal representative, to open bank accounts, to fulfill employment and payroll obligations, and to implement the corporate formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, signing and capitalizing the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: All shareholders and, if applicable, a French notaire; bank issuing the capital blockage certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the French-language statuts for a SARL, specify corporate purpose covering global EOR and cross-border contractor payroll, capital, duration, registered office, and management powers. Each shareholder must sign the statuts. Cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked corporate account at a French bank; in-kind contributions require a commissaire aux apports valuation report unless waived under applicable legal thresholds.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Association (statuts) in French
Bank certificate of blocked funds (attestation de blocage de fonds)
In-kind contribution valuation report, if applicable
Identity documents and addresses of shareholders and proposed Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notaire, bank, or registry queries the articles, correct the wording, re-execute signatures, and provide a revised bank certificate before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the incorporation notice in a legal gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorized in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and publish the mandatory legal announcement containing the corporate name, form, capital, registered office address, corporate purpose, duration, registry where the company will be registered, and the identity of the Gérant. Obtain the publisher's attestation of publication.
required_dossiers: Stated capital and registered office details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is refused, correct the announcement text and re-submit to the same or another authorized JAL; the attestation must be obtained before the M0 filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of the incorporation file with the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), forwarded to the CFE and Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the M0 electronic form on the Guichet Unique, upload the signed statuts, publication attestation, capital blockage certificate, proof of registered-office domiciliation, and manager declarations. The system routes the dossier to the RCS for legal review and registration.
required_dossiers: Copy of valid ID and criminal record attestation for the Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a request for complementary information, respond through the Guichet Unique within 15 calendar days; amend and re-upload any defective annex and confirm legal availability of the company name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and issuance of Kbis and SIREN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office location; INSEE for SIREN/SIRET
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon validation of the M0 dossier, the Registry registers the SARL, assigns the SIREN/SIRET identifiers, and issues the extrait Kbis as the official corporate identity certificate. The bank may then release the blocked funds into the operational account.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registry fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed or refused due to a legal irregularity, apply for judicial rectification before the commercial court or re-file a corrected M0; the Kbis is deemed final upon issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration labor and social security authorizations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DREETS (Direction régionale de l'économie, de l'emploi, du travail et des solidarités) and URSSAF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Kbis issuance, register as an employer with URSSAF and, if the company provides staffing-agency or temporary-work services, file the required declaration of activity with the labor inspectorate, provide the financial guarantee certificate, and confirm compliance with the French declaration of posting rules for cross-border employees.
required_dossiers: DREETS declaration of employment-agency activity, if applicable
Financial guarantee certificate issued by an authorized credit institution or insurance company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DREETS or URSSAF queries the declaration, supplement the dossier with corrected corporate documentation and provide evidence of the guarantee; operations may not commence until the declaration is accepted and registration is effective.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère du Travail / DREETS, Unité de contrôle de l'inspection du travail
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Déclaration préalable d'activité d'agence de placement / travail temporaire and attestation de garantie financière under Labour Code Articles L.124-3 to L.124-10

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique / DREAL (Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / non-ICPE for standard office-based EOR operations; no Full EIA or environmental authorization required unless the company also operates a physical warehouse, motor pool, or other classified facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standard: Office-only activity has no industrial process discharges. If ancillary space is leased, comply with municipal wastewater discharge limits, segregated waste collection, and bordereau de suivi des déchets for any hazardous waste; no VOC or specific industrial emission thresholds applicable to administrative employment-services operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain fire-safety conformity for the registered office as an ERP of the 5th category through a commission de sécurité / SDIS inspection, maintain evacuation plans and fire extinguishers; arrange electrical installation verification and occupational health clearance by a workplace-health service (Service de prévention et de santé au travail); ensure workplace accessibility, adequate sanitary facilities, and employers' social-security compliance for employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), official portal: impots.gouv.fr; corporate formation and registration via Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; customs and export formalities under Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI), portal: douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SARL, statutory incorporation documents are filed through the Guichet Unique (Centre de Formalités des Entreprises). DGFiP issues the SIREN, SIRET, and Registre National des Entreprises registration. VAT identification is automatic for established taxable persons: DGFiP allocates a French intra-Community VAT number (FR + 11 digits) under CGI Article 286 ter, verifiable via the EU VIES system. A non-established foreign enterprise needing direct French VAT registration must submit a registration application to the competent DGFiP local tax office and, if established outside the EU/EEA, appoint an accredited tax representative. A French SARL acting as an Employer of Record is an established taxable person and registers for French VAT from the start of taxable activity without requiring a turnover threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in France. A SARL is by default subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) at entity level. Under CGI Article 239 bis AA, a qualifying SARL may elect, for a maximum of the first five fiscal years and subject to conditions including all shareholders being natural persons, to be taxed transparently as a société de personnes. On indirect taxes, a small business may elect to opt out of the franchise en base de TVA exemption under CGI Article 293 B to become subject to VAT. EU/ATAD hybrid mismatch rules impose notification and disallowance obligations rather than elective classification mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: The general statutory VAT registration/exemption thresholds under the franchise en base de TVA (CGI Article 293 B) are EUR 85,000 for principal activity of supplying goods and EUR 37,500 for supplies of services, with special reduced thresholds applicable to supplies of dwelling-related services and certain liberal professions. These thresholds are exemptions for small taxpayers, not ordinary taxable person registration thresholds: an established SARL carrying on an EOR/staffing business is required to register for VAT from the first euro of taxable activity. Cross-border B2B services supplied to non-French / non-EU customers are subject to place-of-supply rules and reverse charge rather than threshold-based registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is phasing in a mandatory B2B electronic invoicing and e-reporting regime under CGI Article 289 bis. From 1 September 2026, large and mid-size enterprises must receive and issue structured electronic invoices (Factur-X, UBL, CII) through a registered Platforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) or the Public/Portail Public de Facturation (PPF); from 1 September 2027, the obligation extends to small enterprises and micro-enterprises. Cross-border B2B and B2C transactions are covered by e-reporting requirements submitted to DGFiP via API. There is currently no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping for continuous transaction authorization, but all e-invoice data must be transmitted in real time or near-real time to the relevant PDP/PPF for audit and clearance purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies under CGI Article 262.I only to goods physically dispatched or transported by the supplier or on the supplier's behalf to a destination outside the European Union. The exporter must retain documentary proof of export, normally within one year from shipment. EOR and staffing services supplied by a French SARL to non-French or non-EU business customers are not technically zero-rated; they are outside French VAT scope under the B2B place-of-supply rule (reverse charge in the customer's jurisdiction) where the customer is a taxable person. Staffing services supplied to a French-established client remain subject to French VAT at 20%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'exportation - EX / DELTA export system)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport contract
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Proof of physical departure from EU customs territory (port/airport customs records or customs stamps)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP may reclassify improperly zero-rated supplies as taxable domestic supplies and assess VAT at 20% plus late payment interest (0.20% per month) and penalties: 40% where a serious inaccuracy is found, 80% in cases of bad faith, and 100% for fraudulent maneuvers or deliberate dissimulation. Failure to substantiate export within the one-year evidentiary period triggers a retrospective VAT clawback plus interest and penalties. Customs and exchange-control infringements, including false declarations or failure to repatriate export proceeds, may result in administrative fines up to the value of the goods or services involved and, in aggravated cases, criminal sanctions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting within the European System of Central Banks (ESCB); prudential supervision and licensing of banks, payment institutions and electronic-money institutions rest with the ACPR (Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in France. Capital and current account transactions are liberalised under Articles 63-66 TFEU and the French Monetary and Financial Code. France maintains no exchange-control authorisation, no profit-repatriation queue and no blocked-fund mechanisms. Statutory limitation applies only to sectoral foreign-direct-investment screening in strategic activities (defence, security, gambling, public order), which is irrelevant to an EOR payroll scope. Dividend remittances from the FR SARL: an EU parent holding at least 10% for a minimum 2-year period is exempt from French withholding tax under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive; non-EU parents face a 25% withholding tax under Article 119 bis of the French General Tax Code (CGI), reduced by applicable double tax treaties (e.g., 0-5% under the US-France treaty on qualifying holdings). All cross-border flows are traced by the receiving ACPR-licensed intermediary for Banque de France statistical balance-of-payments purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. France does not impose statutory surrender timelines or mandatory conversion ratios for export or service receipts. Euro and foreign-currency proceeds may be retained in accounts with an ACPR-licensed bank or held abroad; the authorised intermediary reports settlement flows to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics. For direct-investment-related inflows from non-EU residents, transactions at or above the Banque de France monthly declaration threshold of EUR 15 million per operation require a dedicated statistical return; smaller inflows are captured by the intermediary's normal reporting. No forced conversion into euro is ever required.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: HIGH for cross-border contractor disbursement and API-based payout rails; MEDIUM for primary treasury hosting. Wise Europe SA (electronic-money institution authorised by the National Bank of Belgium and passported into France) is viable for batch payroll and contractor payments in 40+ currencies; Qonto SAS and Shine (Société Générale) provide French-IBAN accounts with fully remote opening. Legal constraints: (i) EMI balances are safeguarded e-money, not bank deposits, and are outside the French FGDR deposit-guarantee scheme; (ii) an EMI cannot issue the banker's attestation de dépôt de fonds required to certify the SARL's initial capital, so the capital constitution escrow must be held by an ACPR-licensed bank or a notary; (iii) a French bank account is operationally preferable for URSSAF, DGFiP and DSN payroll debits and for the financial-guarantee evidence required by workplace-staffing regulations; (iv) non-EU offshore EMIs without an EEA passport or French agent cannot lawfully serve as the SARL's statutory corporate treasury account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French AML law permits remote video identification and eKYC under the transposed 5th EU AML Directive. In practice, tier-1 French banks still require a physical interview for (i) the gérant (manager) of a newly formed SARL, (ii) any non-EU or offshore UBO, and (iii) accounts intended for FX derivative execution or high transaction volumes. Fully remote opening is generally available only through fintechs (Qonto, Shine) or where the entire management chain is EU-based and the KYC package is introduced by a licensed correspondent. Where the gérant is a foreign non-resident, banks typically require original or apostilled/legalised corporate documents, the RCS Kbis extract, a notarised procuration for local signatories, and a FATCA questionnaire (Form W-8BEN-E or country-specific equivalent) when a US person appears in the ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wholly foreign-owned SARL with a non-EU offshore holding company and no physical French office at onboarding; flagged as a potential shell-company indicator under the French AML framework (Code monétaire et financier, Article L.561-5).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Defence dossier: current Kbis extract (issued within 3 months); certified statuts (articles of association); French RCS beneficial-ownership declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) receipt; apostilled/legalised group structure chart disclosing the full UBO chain; parent company good-standing certificate; audited group financial statements with source-of-funds evidence; detailed French business plan; EOR master services agreement; applicable staffing-activity licence/registration disclosure to DREETS; and proof of registered-office address or service contract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity pass-through treasury pattern: large inbound payments from foreign end-clients followed within days by payroll and contractor outflows to dozens of individuals, creating a potential unauthorised money-service business or conduit risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Defence dossier: payroll governance pack comprising DSN (Déclaration Sociale Nominative) transmissions, payslips, URSSAF contribution receipts, end-client invoices, per-headcount scoping statements, French employment contracts, the EOR platform agreement, a four-eyes payment authorisation matrix, and periodic transaction-monitoring reports produced by the appointed compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border contractor beneficiaries located in high-risk or sanctioned-adjacent jurisdictions, paid through digital EMIs (e.g., Wise) with limited source-of-funds documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Defence dossier: per-contractor ISIC 7810 services agreements; identity verification and sanctions-screening evidence against EU, OFSI and OFAC lists; contractor risk ratings; commercial rationale memorandum; evidence that no beneficiary is a PEP or designated person; batch-wise reconciliation of contractor payouts to underlying end-client invoices; and complete SWIFT/API transfer records retained for at least 10 years under French commercial-law evidentiary rules.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial capital: transfer EUR by SEPA (within the EU) or by SWIFT MT103 (non-EU) to the SARL's blocked capital account (compte bloqué) maintained with the chosen ACPR-licensed bank or held by a notary in a sequestrated account; the MT103 field 70 narrative should read 'CONSTITUTION DE CAPITAL - SARL [NAME]'. The depositary bank issues the attestation de dépôt de fonds required for RCS/Kbis registration. Subsequent injections: the shareholder passes a resolution (P.V. d'assemblée) and the statuts are updated; the transfer narrative must state 'AUGMENTATION DE CAPITAL' or 'AVANCE EN COMPTE COURANT D'ASSOCIÉ'. The receiving bank automatically reports the flow to the Banque de France as part of balance-of-payments statistics and performs EU/OFAC sanctions screening and UBO verification. Non-EU direct-investment inflows of EUR 15 million or more per operation trigger a specific monthly statistical declaration to the Banque de France; no prior ministry or central-bank authorisation is required for an EOR payroll business.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic payroll: the French payroll engine files SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT) and, where required, SEPA Instant Credit Transfers (SCT Inst up to EUR 100,000) for same-day salary crediting; DSN filings fund URSSAF social contributions directly from the operational account. French employees are paid exclusively in EUR from the French IBAN. Cross-border contractor settlements: SWIFT MT103 transfers (beneficiary receives in local currency with shared or half charges) or API-based EMI rails (e.g., Wise Batch) converting EUR at interbank-linked rates, with each payout referencing the underlying contractor agreement and payroll ledger line. For goods/trade settlement if any (e.g., equipment, licences), the French bank can issue an irrevocable documentary letter of credit under ICC UCP 600, with optional confirmation by the beneficiary's correspondent bank. All outflows are reconciled to the payroll register and retained for VAT, transfer-pricing and French commercial-law audit requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (change à terme) on EUR/USD, EUR/GBP and other liquid pairs with an ACPR-licensed bank under an ISDA 1998 FX or FBF (Fédération Bancaire Française) Master Agreement, subject to EMIR trade reporting.
FX swaps (combined spot and forward legs) for monthly payroll liquidity management across currencies, documented under the same ISDA/FBF framework.
Cross-currency swaps (XCCY) for multi-year euro versus foreign-currency net exposure (typically EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) with applicable EMIR margin and collateral rules.
European-style vanilla FX options (purchase only) as premium-limited hedges on material payroll-currency exposures, requiring evidence of underlying treasury exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for blocked or exotic currencies (e.g., BRL, NGN, ARS) may be offered by the bank's trading desk when the EOR's contractor payout in that currency cannot be physically delivered, provided a genuine payroll exposure is demonstrated; NDFs on EUR are not standard because the euro is freely deliverable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual financial statements and allocation of profit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SARL shareholders; no filing authority at approval stage
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of each financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential court injunction, personal liability of the manager, and administrative fine for late accounts filing. No automatic strike-off deadline applies solely to late approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts and related corporate documents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry (Greffe du tribunal de commerce) or competent business court registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after shareholder approval, or within 2 months where filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine generally up to EUR 1,500, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance; court injunction and possible ex officio removal from the commercial register after formal notice. France has no fixed automatic strike-off period for this default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Form 2065 and financial tax schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by the second business day after 1 May for a calendar-year company; otherwise within 3 months after financial year-end, subject to the applicable electronic filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest generally 0.20% per month and a 10% surcharge, increasing in aggravated cases; tax reassessment and collection measures may follow. No administrative strike-off is automatically triggered.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return and payment, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual CA12 return for the simplified regime, or monthly or quarterly CA3 returns under the normal regime; deadlines depend on the applicable VAT regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest, 5% payment penalty in applicable cases, 10% late-filing surcharge, and potential tax audit or reassessment. No administrative strike-off is automatically triggered.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally payable by 15 December annually; advance payment may apply where the prior-year liability exceeds the statutory threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest and collection surcharges under French tax procedure. No annual return is generally required unless specifically requested or a declaration is due for a change in circumstances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Event-driven; file changes to beneficial-owner information without undue delay and generally within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction, criminal penalties for failure or inaccurate filing, and possible restrictions on registry compliance. No standalone annual confirmation filing is required.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory when the SARL exceeds at least 2 of 3 thresholds at financial year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional group-based audit rules may apply where the SARL controls or is controlled by qualifying entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority (Autorité des normes comptables). IFRS is not generally mandatory for standalone SARL statutory accounts; IFRS may apply to qualifying consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a separate annual UBO confirmation. The SARL must maintain accurate beneficial-owner information and file changes through the commercial registry, generally within 30 days of the change. Share transfers and ownership changes must also be documented and reflected in the relevant corporate records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholder decisions and management decisions
Register or file of shareholders, share transfers, and ownership documentation
Register or file of managers and their appointment and removal documents
Minute book and signed corporate resolutions
Accounting books, annual accounts, and supporting accounting records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 3,500-15,000 per year where a statutory auditor is legally required; otherwise 0 for statutory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (2022 onwards; applicable to all profits exceeding EUR 42,500 for SMEs; loss of 27.5% transition rate not relevant)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs with annual turnover below EUR 10m; no sector-specific corporate tax holiday for EOR/staffing activities; wage costs fully deductible; social charges are deductible but not reducing IS below zero; temporary carryback ('report en arrière') available for 3 years capped at EUR 1m.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: unlimited (no expiry; annual deduction capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable income exceeding that threshold)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire n° 2065 (CERFA n° 27294) for corporate income tax, together with annexes in the official 2065-SD / 2056-2064 set; filed electronically via the EFI service (Espace Professionnel EDI) on impots.gouv.fr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (plus provisional instalments on 15 Mar, 15 Jun, 15 Sep, 15 Dec)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the close of the fiscal year. For fiscal years ending 31 December, the return is generally due by the second working day after 1 May of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identity: legal form, SIREN/SIRET, APE code, registered office, fiscal representative or principal place of business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the French permanent establishment's details; foreign head-office address should be shown only in the 'foreign HQ' field; no foreign company EIN to be entered in the French SIREN box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net profit or loss for the period before fiscal adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report solely the French PE result; do not consolidate foreign head-office revenues or third-party sales booked abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses and add-backs: tax penalties, excessive director fees, unsubstantiated intercompany charges, book depreciation not aligned with fiscal rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back any excessive allocation of head-office overheads to the French PE unless supported by an arm's-length transfer-pricing study.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses used to offset the current year's taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the French PE's own accumulated losses are usable; losses of foreign branch are not available; attach prior-year 2065 filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income or deficit after all add-backs and deductions, carried to the final computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that this amount corresponds to the PE's audited accounts and that no double-counting of withholding tax credits occurs in respect of cross-border income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% automatic increase in assessed corporate tax; late payment interest at 0.2% per month; if the return is filed after a formal demand and within 30 days, additional 20% surcharge; for fraudulent or abusive filings, 80% surcharge; missing annexes attract fines of EUR 150-€200 per form; failure to file electronically additional EUR 500 statutory fee.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% general statutory withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident companies (CGI art. 119 bis 2).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Apply for treaty relief before dividend payment by submitting Form 2766 (or designated local equivalent) and a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the recipient's tax authority. For an EU parent company, obtain advance exemption under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (10% qualifying holding for at least 2 years) by filing the same form and attaching the necessary ownership certificate. If withholding was made at source, a refund claim must be filed with the DDFIP (Direction Départementale des Finances Publiques) within the statutory claim period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 33.33% statutory withholding under French domestic law; treaty rates commonly 5%-10%. Interest: domestic withholding generally 0% for arm's-length interest paid to non-resident banks and commercial lenders; an increased 75% domestic rate applies to payments to entities resident in non-cooperative states (États non coopératifs), subject to treaty override.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR. Annual form 2257 (transfer-pricing declaration) is required when aggregate controlled transactions with foreign related parties exceed EUR 100,000. Full Master File / Local File documentation is mandatory for enterprises whose turnover or balance-sheet total exceeds EUR 400 million, or belonging to a group whose consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 400 million. Country-by-Country reports apply to groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not have a standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime comparable to the UAE. However, the French 'abus de droit' doctrine (LPF art. L64) and the general anti-abuse framework allow the tax administration to disregard artificial arrangements lacking commercial substance. For an EOR, substance must be demonstrable through a French office, local payroll, staff hierarchy, physical asset management, board decisions, and compliance with French labor law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful failure to file the 2065 return, omission of a material part of taxable revenue, or systematic overstatement of deductions and intercompany fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud (CGI art. 1741): up to 5 years' imprisonment and EUR 75,000 fine; administrative surcharges: 40% for bad faith, 80% for fraudulent intent; late-payment interest at 0.2% per month; potential embargo of bank accounts and seizure of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be prosecuted as accomplices for personal participation in the tax evasion. Courts may impose travel bans, corporate-director disqualification, and direct personal recovery of the company's unpaid taxes under the 'action en comblement du passif' if the director's fault caused the insufficiency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: French SARL operated as a letterbox without real employees, premises, independent management, or economic activity; unsubstantiated payment of service fees to an offshore related party.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under LPF art. L64, the tax administration may disregard the transaction or the entire legal structure and recharacterize income as a deemed distribution or as taxable income of the beneficial owner. Penalty: 80% surcharge on the reassessed tax; denied deductibility and reclassification of fees as hidden remuneration; possible 3-year statute extension.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Court may pierce the corporate veil if the company is fictitious or manifestly undercapitalized; director can be held jointly liable for corporate taxes, interest, and penalties, and criminally liable for forgery of books/accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a Global EOR/staffing agency in France without the mandatory authorization from the Ministry of Labour to supply temporary employees or to operate as a recruitment agency (licence préfectorale).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Prohibition of illegal labor lending (prêt illicite de main-d'œuvre) and trafficking of labor (marchandage) under the French Labour Code: up to 5 years' imprisonment and EUR 75,000 fine; administrative fine of EUR 4,000 per illegally supplied worker; suspension of activity by the labor inspectorate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally exposed to criminal penalties and may be banned from managing a company for up to 5 years; social-security authorities may also seek civil recovery of unpaid employer contributions against the director in cases of fraudulent practises.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the company's actual beneficial owner declaration (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) at the commercial registry; failure to report a foreign bank account or payment flow to TRACFIN; use of disguised cross-border payroll transfers lacking documentary trail.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to declare beneficial owner: fine up to EUR 7,500 for a legal entity; unreported foreign bank account: EUR 1,500 per account (EUR 10,000 if the account is held in a non-cooperative state); money laundering (C. pén. art. 324-1): 5 years' imprisonment and EUR 375,000 fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be criminally liable for money laundering and may face asset freezing, travel ban, and personal confiscation orders; civil liability extends to monetary fines and restitution of illegal profits; AML governance failures may lead to a management ban by the regulatory authority.
